title: WHAT THE DATA SAY: 56% of CEOs say their organizations aren’t speaking up enough on issues
body_markdown:
By: Ray Day


## **CONTACT:**


Ray Day
ray.day@stagwellglobal.com


*We wanted to share our latest consumer and business insights, based on research from[Stagwell](https://www.stagwellglobal.com/) and[Allison Worldwide](https://www.allisonworldwide.com/) .* *Among the highlights of our weekly* *consumer sentiment tracking:*


**CEOs WANT COMMS TO SPEAK UP MORE, WITH MORE HUMANITY**


CEOs want their organizations to speak up more and add more humanity in communications, according to the sixth annual survey of CEOs and communications leaders from[HarrisX and Ragan](https://www.ragan.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/HarrisX-Ragan-SurveyofCEOs-Communications-Leaders-2026.pdf) .


- 56% of CEOs say their organizations aren’t speaking up enough on issues, up from 42% in 2025 – when 58% said they were speaking up too much.
- CEOs see company community investments (83%), hires and promotions (78%) and paid family leave policies (74%) as safe topics to discuss.
- Transgender rights (67%), election results (65%) and race relations (65%) are seen as risky topics to discuss as a business.
- 95% of organizations use AI in communications, and 48% are actively investing in and integrating it, up from 40% last year.
- 75% of leaders say AI is largely delivering on its promise of faster, better and more efficient communications.
- 7 in 10 CEOs say great communications professionals are still needed in the AI era, just with new tools – up from 51% last year.
- More than half (52%) would trust a top-tier professional without AI support over a custom-trained AI tool to write an important speech.
- In a reputational crisis, 62% of leaders favor responding to set the record straight, even if doing so draws more attention.
- 63% say market research provides the clearest picture of an issue’s broader reputational impact.
- Yet, among organizations that have faced a crisis, 72% used social media metrics to guide the response, while only 35% used market research.
- *See also:*[Midterms Underscore Capitalism’s Growing PR Problem](https://justcapital.com/news/americans-views-on-business-2026/?utm_campaign=34495300-EMAIL%20-%20Newsletter%20-%20ATW%20-%202026&utm_medium=email&_hsenc=p2ANqtz-_MfO92V_x7LOwVyxA1iqiHSE5NcgI6-iXbYxfYgrFjFiGPO7XcEa-G0oRR1pLMj7r9fqCiVr-koAA59xHCt01np0J7AjpFLtktubLHJe_Y8F_VgpY&_hsmi=450254169&utm_content=450254169&utm_source=hs_email#key-findings)


**HEALTHCARE NEEDS A TRANSLATOR**


Americans are struggling to understand healthcare information and see a role for AI in making it simpler – yet not for diagnoses – according to new research from The Harris Poll and[Elevance Health](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261117375801/en/From-Confusion-to-Clarity-Consumers-See-a-Role-for-AI-in-Simplifying-Healthcare-Elevance-HealthHarris-Poll-Survey-Finds) .


- 82% say some part of healthcare information feels like a “foreign language.”
- 45% have made a healthcare decision they later regretted because they didn’t understand the basics.
- Nearly three-quarters have encountered a healthcare challenge, such as understanding insurance coverage or a medical bill.
- Only 27% of those with a health plan say they completely understand it.
- 82% wish they could secure healthcare answers as fast as they can order food delivery through an app.
- 83% want an easy way to receive personalized healthcare recommendations based on factors such as their insurance, health needs and financial situation.
- 79% believe AI can improve healthcare experiences overall, yet only 20% currently use it as a regular healthcare information source.
- 72% would trust AI to accurately provide at least one type of healthcare information. However, trust varies by task: 33% trust it to explain insurance benefits, 30% to estimate healthcare costs and 13% for a diagnosis.
- *See also* : *[A doctor’s office or on-call doctor are considered a trusted resource by 81% of Baby Boomers but just 39% of Gen Z](https://markets.businessinsider.com/news/stocks/survey-reveals-care-navigation-gap-when-patients-must-decide-when-and-where-to-get-help-1036779066)*


**CREDIT FOR CHRISTMAS**


More Americans expect to need credit to cover monthly expenses heading into peak holiday shopping season, according to NerdWallet’s November[Consumer Financial Resilience Index](https://www.nerdwallet.com/finance/studies/financial-resilience-index) , conducted by The Harris Poll.


- 41% expect to rely on credit for at least some November expenses, up from 35% in September – a statistically significant 6-point increase.
- Millennials (57%) and Gen Z adults (52%) are most likely to need credit, compared with 39% of Gen X and 21% of Boomers.
- 58% of parents with children younger than 18 expect to rely on credit this month, versus 34% of Americans without minor children.
- About one-third lack a $1,000 emergency cash cushion.
- Despite rising credit needs, 77% feel in control of their day-to-day finances, and the same share are confident they can pay all their bills on time this month.
- 63% believe the U.S. economy will enter a recession within the next year, including 73% of millennials, 69% of Gen Xers, 59% of Gen Z adults and 52% of baby boomers.
- The overall Financial Resilience Index score stands at 60.9 out of 100, compared with 61.6 in October and 61.5 in September.
- *See also:*[New Year, New Me Is Starting Before 2027](https://www.nerdwallet.com/finance/studies/winter-arc-survey?utm_campaign=34495300-EMAIL%20-%20Newsletter%20-%20ATW%20-%202026&utm_medium=email&_hsenc=p2ANqtz-9GkKcPIeqXaV_aXALINIM8zbThVOyORTE1x8fdawvowrFyD71l3nIsfovFhGlL1-NPpCxga59O-so5G0Mq10bZ0zExbquQUKSGmopUqSeTmPnn5HI&_hsmi=450254169&utm_content=450254169&utm_source=hs_email)
